title: Linear-vs-free step navigation is a per-project elicit; the task-list respects it by disabling out-of-order entry on linear and permitting it on free
asA: operator whose project has committed to a step order posture
iWant: the task-list to disable step links whose prerequisites are unfinished when the project runs linear, or to permit any step at any time when the project runs free
soThat: the surface matches the project's committed posture and does not let me enter a step whose prerequisites the domain forbids

acceptanceCriteria.description: On the ?nav=linear branch, task-list rows whose [data-step-state] is Cannot start yet render as non-anchor spans (no clickable href) and the pack asserts a click on the row does not change the URL. On the ?nav=free branch every row renders as an anchor and a click on any row navigates to that step's route. ADR-2501 records the elicit and the shipped default is linear.

Alternative step-indicator contracts drawn from the closed set owned by `ADR-2503.decision` each render exactly the contract for the elicited option; a value outside the owned set refuses at apply with STEP_INDICATOR_UNKNOWN naming the value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project elicits a step-indicator outside the closed set
acceptanceCriteria.then: apply exits with a non-zero code and STEP_INDICATOR_UNKNOWN names the value; each option in the set owned by `ADR-2503.decision` renders its own contract
